title: Fourteen Winters and One Short Candle
subtitle: 信念信仰 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 信念信仰（人与自我·做人与做事）
meta: 主题语境：信念信仰（人与自我·做人与做事）　|　核心词汇：faith　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 faith 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1912 my great-aunt ① kept a faith that no neighbour in the village would have named, and she said the keeping was the whole of the winter. The ② faith, meaning the belief itself and not the church, ran fourteen winters and stayed unnamed in the book; a faith, she said, is the only thing in a village that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ faith in that village had the same short candle beside it, and the ④ faith at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A faith, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to name; my great-aunt said the naming is the part that fills fourteen winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the faith was the whole of the promise, meaning the trust and not the belief. The ⑥ faith, meaning the trust and not any of that, is the only thing in a promise that everybody waits for and nobody names; faith, he said, is either something you keep or the only word that means both a belief and trust. He said the trust is the part they remember.

By 1920 the ⑦ faith had become a line in a letter, and the letter had become an argument about the short candle. The ⑧ faith of the whole thing, my great-aunt wrote in January, was one village and fourteen winters of naming; faith, she said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to name. She said the naming was never mentioned.

The ⑨ faith I remember is the one named in the letter, which closed in 1926 and is still described as the quietest in the village. A ⑩ faith, my mother said in 1928, is the only one that improves by being named; every faith, she said, is trust that has agreed to look like a belief. She said the trust was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 信念；信仰（指村子里每一种旁边的那一种）
B. n. 信仰（指那一种本身，与教堂相对）
C. 固定搭配：keep a faith 坚守一种信仰
D. n. 信仰（指留给孩子的那一种）
E. n. 信仰（抽象总称，指一座村子的信仰之事）
F. n. 信仰（指信上写到、被说出的那一种）
G. n. 信任；信赖（指一个承诺里人人都等却无人说出的那样东西）
H. n. 信任（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人说出的那样东西）

items.q: kept a faith that no neighbour in the village would have named
The faith, meaning the belief itself and not the church
the faith at the far side
the faith was the whole of the promise
the faith had become a line in a letter
The faith of the whole thing
A faith, my mother said in 1928

answers.why: keep a faith 意为“坚守一种信仰”，1912 年姑婆坚守了一种村子里没有一位邻居肯说出的信仰。
faith 意为“信仰”，指那一种本身而不是教堂，它经过了十四个冬天而在簿子上没有名字。
faith 意为“信念、信仰”，指村子里每一种旁边的那一种，每一种旁边都有同一支短短的蜡烛。
faith 意为“信仰”，指留给孩子的那一种，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
faith 意为“信任、信赖”，指一个承诺里人人都等却无人说出的那样东西，叔叔说这份信任就是那个承诺的全部。
faith 意为“信任”，指人人都等却无人说出的那样东西而不是那一种信仰，是承诺里人人都等、却无人说出的东西。
faith 意为“信仰”，指信上写到、被说出的那一种，到 1920 年这一种成了信里的一行。
faith 意为“信仰”，姑婆一月写道，整件事的信仰之事是一座村子和十四个冬天的说出。
faith 意为“信仰”，我记得的是信上说出的那一种，1926 年结束了，至今仍被说成村子里最安静的一种。
faith 为抽象总称，母亲 1928 年说，一种信仰是唯一会因为被好好说出而变得更好的东西。
